key_insight: AMIFound is a single foundation model that can restore and enhance medical images across seven different imaging modalities. It improves image quality while preserving clinically important details needed for diagnosis.
problem_solved: Medical images often suffer from modality-specific degradations such as noise, blur, low contrast, and artifacts. Existing restoration methods are usually built for one imaging type or one degradation, making them hard to scale and less robust in clinical settings.
method: Trains one unified foundation model to handle multiple medical imaging modalities instead of separate task-specific models.
Learns to restore images under a range of degradation types, aiming for generalization across diverse clinical acquisition conditions.
Focuses on enhancing image quality while maintaining diagnostic structures and medically relevant information.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that a single scalable model can replace many specialized restoration pipelines in medical imaging. It points toward more efficient deployment, better cross-modality robustness, and clinically safer enhancement systems.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing multiple input modalities feeding into one AMIFound model and producing restored outputs

paper_title: An all-in-one foundation model for multimodal medical image restoration and enhancement
paper_authors: Luyang Cao, Zhijian Wu, Jian Zhang, Lei Qi, Yang Gao
